correction: Selecting a palette row must also scroll the list to it: Show and a changed query reset Selected to 0 but kept the ListState offset, so after Down 35 times, Escape and Ctrl K the list showed commands 22 to 39 while Enter ran command 0, off screen

A per-line contract must be applied per line: ConsoleWriter called Classify once on a whole write and Console.Add split the text under that one level, so with an ERROR-prefix classifier the write "okay\nERROR failed\n" recorded both lines as Info and the reverse order counted an ordinary line as an error; the writer now splits the write and classifies each line

Jobs.Find must follow Enqueue order to return the newest job of a source and key: it returned the running job first and then searched the queue oldest-first, so with A running and B of the same pair queued it returned A; it now searches the queue newest-first, then the running job, then the batch, and Pending checks the running and queued jobs itself, so a newer job dropped by CancelAll does not hide an Unstoppable one still running

OpenGeneration must use its own membership snapshot, not probe for a future MyGo Selection.Generation method that a dependency bump could silently activate with unchecked semantics. Adopt dependency APIs explicitly with compatibility tests.

A ui.Handle must never be made in a view or with ui.Local: its first Bind appends a registration to the window's refs that nothing removes until the window closes, and applyFocusRequests walks them all every build pass. SourceList made one per row mount with ui.Local for OnMiddleClick, so every row that scrolled back into view or reappeared as its section opened leaked one; the list now keeps the middle press in its own fields and the row's ObserveInput, by MyGo's hit test, tells that the release is over the row (which also stops a release over a pinned section header from clicking the row under it)

A top bar's trailing controls (End, the console's button, the main menu) must never shrink or sit in a clipped container narrower than they are: PaneShell drew them, with the palette field, in the last pane's clipped segment, so a right pane 200 DIPs wide under 110 DIPs of window controls put the field under the controls and the main menu out of the window. Shrink(0) inside the segment cannot fix it (the segment has 66 DIPs, the console's button and the menu take 108), so the bar's end is now the window's, drawn once over the segments, and the field turns compact below its least width; the plain bar and Shell's bar had the same overflow and now keep their trailing controls whole too

Opener passed mailto links to the mail client whole, so a link in a message or a note could carry attach= or other headers some clients act on: the parameter rule assigned to the kit in the review never shipped. A mailto filter keeps only to, cc, bcc, subject and body, compared by their names as written (never decoded, so %61ttach and %74o are dropped), and also drops the fragment: mailto has none, and a client that does not split one off reads ?subject=x#&attach=/etc/passwd as an attach field

The initial MyGo InstalledApps launcher assumed menu-visible entries were the same as launchable desktop IDs and that a running MyGo app was always available. InstalledApps filters NoDisplay entries and requires App.Run. The launcher now resolves IDs through GIO without either restriction.
evidence: frostyard/frostui#21 review by bketelsen (2026-11-12); MyGo v0.9.0 internal/linux/apps.go Applications and app.go needsApp; TestLaunchDesktopApp launches a NoDisplay entry before App.Run

correction: The first GIO launcher was assumed to preserve gtk-launch's detached output behavior. g_app_info_launch actually passed the caller's stdout and stderr through to launched apps, holding pipelines open and mixing app output into the caller's logs. The manager launch now discards both streams.
evidence: frostyard/frostui#21 review by bketelsen (2026-11-12), pipeline measurement; TestLaunchDesktopApp checks stdout and stderr are not inherited

correction: The launch test assumed one FIFO open/read/close cycle captured exactly one launched app. If two writers arrived before the reader reopened, one read consumed both signals and the second open waited forever. The reader now holds the FIFO open and reads two newline-delimited signals.
evidence: frostyard/frostui#21 verify job 130930960968 failed TestLaunchDesktopApp after 5 seconds; TestLaunchDesktopApp -count=100 passes with a persistent FIFO reader

correction: A ui.Handle kept in a map holds its registration until the window closes: dropping the map entry does not release it, so AGENTS.md no longer offers one handle per item of a pruned map. The handle guard read syntax only and never resolved a named type, so a Handle inside a struct of the package was not seen: a ui.Local whose init returns rowState, var st rowState, new(rowState), make of a named slice of Handles, a struct embedding one, an alias of a Handle. It now resolves the package's named types, by value and recursively, with a visited set against cycles
evidence: frostyard/frostui#10, from the cross-review of frostyard/frostui#9 (https://github.com/frostyard/frostui/pull/9#pullrequestreview-5858739862)

correction: The first resolution of named types matched names without the declaring file's import name, kept 1 of several build-tag declarations, and ignored type parameters and function-local types; the guard now reads each declaration in its own file and scope and checks every alternative; a function's local types now follow Go's block scope by source position, since a function-wide local scope hid package types
evidence: frostyard/frostui#23 cross-review at bd6ea5a (openai/gpt-6.1-sol): 3 blocking findings; re-review 1 at 143097a: local types hid package types outside their block
